assertions_contracts.best_practice: The assert discipline itself still holds, but C23 standardises much of what the guide gates: static_assert harmonisation, [[nodiscard]], nullptr, constexpr objects, typeof, #embed, and <stdckdint.h> checked arithmetic are core C23, available via -std=c23 since Clang 18.
assertions_contracts.evidence: WG14 states C23 is the current standard; Clang's C23 feature table lists these features with Clang versions 9-21, i.e. broadly implemented, not speculative.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert()/_Static_assert for internal invariants only, never for external validation, because NDEBUG strips assert; C23 checked arithmetic treated as an optional gated extra.

bounded_work.best_practice: Deliberately stricter than mainstream C practice (TigerBeetle/Power-of-Ten lineage); no official guidance contradicts explicit resource budgets. Newer C only adds helpers (see assertions_contracts).
bounded_work.evidence: Clang's C status page shows incremental C23/C2y safety helpers arriving feature-by-feature, none of which removes the need for explicit caps.
bounded_work.guide_position: Every loop/retry/queue/size/depth bounded by named *_MAX constants; count, item size, cumulative bytes and retry amplification budgeted separately; checked multiplication before allocation.

concurrency.best_practice: Matches the C11/C23 memory model as maintained by WG14; C2y work (e.g. stricter alignment for atomic types) is incremental and does not change the guide's protocol-level advice.
concurrency.evidence: Clang's status page tracks C2y atomic-alignment work as a small increment on the existing model; no official source endorses volatile-as-synchronisation or tolerates data races.
concurrency.guide_position: Documented pthread/C11-atomic protocol, volatile is not synchronisation, data races are UB, async-signal-safe handlers only, shutdown/join/lifetime defined before workers start.

error_handling.best_practice: POSIX and Linux practice agree: errno is per-call and clobbered by cleanup, partial transfers are normal, and Linux close-after-EINTR semantics make blind retry unsafe.
error_handling.evidence: No official source contradicts the guide; its treatment matches the POSIX specification it cites and standard Linux guidance.
error_handling.guide_position: Documented status enum + output parameters, outputs unchanged on failure, errno captured immediately, partial I/O and EINTR handled, no blind retry of close after EINTR on Linux.

formatting.best_practice: clang-format remains the standard formatter for C; all four pinned options are current, documented style options. The 4-space/100-col values are house policy, not an upstream default, and the guide says so.
formatting.evidence: clang-tidy/clang-format documentation in the current LLVM tree still documents the same style-option mechanism and presets, including LLVM.
formatting.guide_position: Pinned clang-format: BasedOnStyle LLVM, IndentWidth 4, ColumnLimit 100, UseTab Never; never reformat vendored code.

memory_ownership.best_practice: C still has no language ownership model; disciplined manual ownership plus static analysis remains the official-ecosystem answer. MISRA C:2025 continues to require freedom from undefined/critical unspecified behaviour rather than any ownership mechanism.
memory_ownership.evidence: MISRA C:2025 is the current critical-systems guideline (Mar 2025) and is built around UB avoidance and tool enforcement, consistent with the guide's manual discipline.
memory_ownership.guide_position: One owner per buffer/fd/handle, one cleanup path (goto acceptable), reverse-order release, realloc via temporary, no pointer into automatic storage escapes, (NULL,0) policy per API.

security.best_practice: Aligns with CERT C practice as mechanically enforced by clang-tidy's cert-* checks and with MISRA C:2025's security-relevant rules; no official guidance has moved toward the constructs the guide bans.
security.evidence: clang-tidy documents a dedicated cert-* group for CERT Secure Coding Guidelines; MISRA C:2025 addenda map the guidelines to CWE memory-safety weaknesses, the same defect classes the guide targets.
security.guide_position: Fixed format strings, bounds-checked copies (strncpy is not a safe strcpy), unsigned char for ctype, no system()/popen() on external input, argv form, openat2-style race-resistant filesystem handling, sanitizer findings treated as real defects.

static_analysis.best_practice: clang-tidy plus the Clang Static Analyzer is the official LLVM static-analysis route, with check groups that map directly onto this guide's rules: cert-* (CERT C), bugprone-*, concurrency-*, and clang-analyzer-*; clangd can also surface clang-tidy diagnostics.
static_analysis.evidence: The clang-tidy documentation lists the cert, bugprone, concurrency and clang-analyzer groups and explains that it also runs Clang Static Analyzer checks; none of this is wired into the guide's pairing or workflow.
static_analysis.guide_position: SKILL toolchain pairing is clangd + clang-format + lldb-dap only; the full guide mentions sanitizers and 'targeted static analysis' generically but names no linter/analyzer or check set.

testing.best_practice: Clang's sanitizer documentation continues to present ASan/UBSan exactly as the guide uses them: defect detectors for exercised paths, not proofs of absence of UB.
testing.evidence: The guide's own cited Clang sanitizer pages remain the current official docs for the LLVM 22 series toolchain it pairs with.
testing.guide_position: Boundary/allocation-failure/interruption/integer-edge tests, fuzz byte parsers behind a size cap, ASan/UBSan runs, a separate TSan build for concurrent code, and a full -DNDEBUG run so tests do not vanish with assert.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: C23 (ISO/IEC 9899:2024) is the current standard. GCC 15+ defaults to gnu23 and GCC 16 is current; Clang has offered -std=c23 since Clang 18. A C17 baseline is now two years behind the published standard and behind both compilers' defaults.
toolchain_pins.evidence: WG14 homepage: the current C standard is C23, adopted 2024. GCC 15 changes page documents the C23-based default change; Clang status page lists -std=c23 as available (partial conformance, feature-by-feature).
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Primary target is ISO C17; C23 features are gated extras behind feature checks; validation recipes compile with -std=c17.

current_versions.C (ISO/IEC 9899): C23 (ISO/IEC 9899:2024) is the current standard per WG14; work on the next revision (C2y) is in draft
current_versions.Clang/LLVM: LLVM 22.1.x series current (22.1.8 seen Sep 2026); Clang status pages list -std=c23 since Clang 18 and -std=c2y partial
current_versions.GCC: GCC 16.1 (Apr 2026); GCC 15+ defaults C to gnu23 (C23-based); -fhardened remains version/platform dependent as the guide warns
current_versions.MISRA C: MISRA C:2025 (Mar 2025) is the current edition; covers C90/C99/C11/C18, not C23
current_versions.clang-format: Ships with LLVM 22.1.x; BasedOnStyle/IndentWidth/ColumnLimit/UseTab options all still valid
current_versions.clang-tidy: Current with LLVM 22.1.x; includes cert-*, bugprone-*, concurrency-*, clang-analyzer-* check groups; NOT paired in the guide
current_versions.clangd: Ships with LLVM 22.1.x; guide pairs it, version not pinned in guide
current_versions.lldb-dap: Ships with LLVM/LLDB 22.1.x as the DAP adapter

mechanical_fixes.correct: **Primary target:** ISO C23 core (ISO/IEC 9899:2024); features beyond the pinned compiler's verified C23 subset gated by feature checks; POSIX/Linux adapters isolated
mechanical_fixes.current: **Primary target:** ISO C17 core; optional C23 features explicitly gated; POSIX/Linux adapters isolated
mechanical_fixes.evidence: WG14 states C23 is the current C standard, adopted by ISO/IEC in 2024; the C17 profile is a superseded standard.

mechanical_fixes.correct: Declare the contract up front: C standard (C23; gate any feature beyond the pinned compiler's verified subset on a feature check, not a compiler flag)
mechanical_fixes.current: Declare the contract up front: C standard (C17; gate C23 features on a feature check, not a compiler flag)
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Same WG14 source: C23 is current; Clang offers -std=c23 since Clang 18 and GCC 15+ defaults to gnu23, so gating all of C23 is no longer the conservative default.
The §27 validation recipe (and its -DNDEBUG companion, also -std=c17) still compiles the reference module as C17 while the current standard and both major compilers' defaults are C23-based.

mechanical_fixes.correct: [WG14 C23 draft N3220 / ISO/IEC 9899:2024, foundational C semantics; C23 profile used here](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n3220.pdf)
mechanical_fixes.current: [WG14 public C11 draft, foundational C semantics; C17 profile used here](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf)
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Source [C1] is cited throughout for core semantics but points at the C11 draft (N1570); WG14's project page lists N3220 as the draft similar to the published C23 standard.

proposals.evidence: clang-tidy is the official LLVM linter, runs the static analyzer's checks, and its cert-*/bugprone-* groups mechanically enforce several rules this guide currently leaves to human review; the guide pairs no linter at all.
proposals.proposal: Add clang-tidy (with the Clang Static Analyzer checks) to the SKILL toolchain pairing and workflow, with a named starter check set (bugprone-*, cert-*, clang-analyzer-*, concurrency-*) run alongside the existing ASan/UBSan step.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt: highest-leverage gap in the C guide. Keep the check set explicit and pinned like the clang-format config.

proposals.evidence: Clang's C23 table shows these features implemented across Clang 9-21 (nodiscard Clang 9, nullptr Clang 17, constexpr objects Clang 19, stdckdint shipped with GCC 15's C23 library support), so they are portable in practice, not paper features.
proposals.proposal: On the C23 baseline, promote the standardised contracts vocabulary from gated extras to defaults where the pinned compiler supports them: [[nodiscard]] on status returns, nullptr, constexpr objects for bounds constants, and <stdckdint.h> checked arithmetic as an alternative to hand-rolled SIZE_MAX division checks.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt incrementally, one feature per project, with the guide's existing feature-check discipline retained for anything beyond the verified subset.
